dimensions.name: Protocol & data-shape orientation

evidence.note: Systematic survey across all six task types: lists /app, /app/tasks, /app/datasets; reads one config per type (classification_01, clustering_03, pair_classification_01, retrieval_01, sts_01, summarization_01); inspects dataset dir structure and head -2 rows for each type including retrieval queries/corpus/qrels.

Reads run_eval.py, cats all 37 task configs, and step 8 explicitly notes samples_per_label overrides may differ across classification configs; step 9 checks dataset sizes and available packages — cataloguing variation before implementing.

Actively reconciles computed main_scores against known MTEB all-MiniLM-L6-v2 leaderboard numbers (BIOSSES 0.816≈0.8166, TwitterURL 0.847≈0.848, SprintDuplicate 0.946≈0.947) to anchor expected outputs — the anchor-8 leaderboard cross-reference behavior.

Engages with the summarization per-prediction skip edge case, but reactively during debugging (0.2596 vs ~0.305) rather than pre-identifying it from inspection; ends rationalizing the gap rather than fully resolving — short of the exhaustive edge-case pre-identification of anchor 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performed a genuine systematic survey of configs and data across all six task types (steps 2-9), catalogued at least one override class (samples_per_label, step 8), and actively reconciled computed scores against MTEB leaderboard numbers throughout implementation (steps 29-41), which squarely matches anchor 8. It does not reach 10 because the deeper edge-case handling (summarization per-prediction skip) surfaced reactively during debugging rather than as pre-identified gotchas grounded in file inspection, and there is no evidence of an exhaustive per-task override catalogue for ignore_identical_ids, max_fraction, or min/max_score.

dimensions.name: Per-type / per-dataset milestone structure

evidence.note: Systematic exploration phase sampling one config+dataset per task type, establishing the six-protocol hierarchy as the implicit structure — but no explicit ordered milestone plan with done-conditions is articulated up front.

Wrote all six task-type implementations in a single continuous authoring pass (append after append), rather than building/verifying a shared encode+similarity core first — the opposite of the risk-sequenced anchor-10 approach.

Validated per task type in sequence (sts → summarization → pair_classification → classification → clustering → retrieval), each with a concrete leaderboard done-check (e.g. sts_01 0.816≈BIOSSES 0.8166; pair_03 0.847≈0.8478). This is genuine type-by-type milestone gating on numeric agreement.

Rough ordering by size/risk: 'test with a small task first', small types before retrieval; retrieval (largest corpora) done last and split per-dataset to checkpoint — practical ordering rationale, not just 'easy ones first'.
37-dataset coverage checked only at the very end (confirmed all 37 present + structural keys); no separate explicit milestone for the CLI contract or skip-and-continue harness behavior.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly splits work by the six task types and validates each type against the MTEB leaderboard before moving on, with concrete numeric done-checks per type — this is stronger than anchor 5's 'plan to validate each type' and reaches into anchor 8's 'done-check tied to leaderboard agreement.' However, it lacks an explicit up-front ordered milestone plan, builds all protocols in one authoring pass rather than sequencing a shared core by risk (anchor 10), and never treats the CLI contract or skip-and-continue behavior as separate milestones (part of anchor 8). This places it solidly between 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness verification against leaderboard/spec

evidence.note: Cross-checked STS_01 (BIOSSES) 0.816 against MTEB leaderboard ~0.8166, and validated the other STS scores against MTEB as they came in — systematic leaderboard comparison, not just eyeballing.

Checked pair_classification scores against specific MTEB numbers (TwitterURLCorpus ~0.8478, SprintDuplicate ~0.947, TwitterSemEval ~0.681) and treated matches as confirmation — per-dataset external reference targets.

Flagged summarization 0.2596 vs leaderboard ~0.305 as a suspected bug and investigated candidate protocol steps (predicted-skip logic, gold normalization, dot≈cosine) to localize the divergence — isolating to a specific protocol detail, though ultimately concluded 0.2596 'is correct' without full resolution.

Listed expected per-dataset classification scores (MTOPDomain ~0.83, Banking77 ~0.66, etc.) against the 8 computed values to sanity-check — reference comparison, but done reactively after the run rather than established up front.

Re-examined the summarization discrepancy at the end but never built micro-tests for tricky behaviors (shuffle composition, bootstrap sampling counts, negation signs) and did not verify secondary metrics systematically; clustering/retrieval scores only lightly eyeballed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond the level-5 anchor: it compared main_scores for many datasets across STS, pair_classification, and classification against specific all-MiniLM-L6-v2 leaderboard values and treated the summarization deviation as a bug, tracing it toward specific protocol steps (skip logic, gold normalization). But it falls short of level 8: reference values were checked reactively rather than established up front, verification centered on main_score rather than secondary metrics, no targeted micro-tests localized the tricky sub-behaviors, clustering/retrieval were only eyeballed, and the summarization discrepancy was rationalized away rather than resolved.

dimensions.name: 37-task pass/fail tracking

evidence.note: Immediately established the scope ('37 tasks total') and organized exploration by type, giving a coverage baseline to track against.
Tracked per-type completion as it went — 'All 9 STS tasks done', 'All 8 classifications done', 'All clustering done' — a running done-vs-remaining picture across the six types.

After Ctrl+C on the long retrieval run, checked results.json keys and precisely identified 'Got 6 of 10 retrievals. Need to do 07-10', then ran the missing ones individually to checkpoint — accurate detection of partial coverage.
Noticed summarization 0.2596 vs leaderboard ~0.305 divergence, probed it a couple times, then explicitly re-prioritized ('Move on for now') rather than looping indefinitely on one protocol.
Final reconciliation: counted len(r)=37 tasks and confirmed all had required keys / valid numbers, verifying full coverage before submitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently kept a running per-type tally of done-vs-remaining, and notably at steps 55-56 detected exactly which retrieval datasets were missing from results.json and filled them in, plus verified all 37 present at the end — clearly above anchor 5's 'running list + periodic coverage confirmation.' It also showed anchor-8 traits by noticing the summarization divergence and re-prioritizing instead of thrashing. However, tracking was mental/ad hoc rather than an explicit updated ledger, and numerical-confirmation status was spot-checked per type rather than reconciled per-dataset (final 'complete' rested on structural keys, not per-metric confirmation), so it falls short of the full anchor 8/10, landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Debugging protocol divergences

evidence.note: STS_01 score 0.816 cross-checked against MTEB (~0.8166) and confirmed matching — a verification pass, no divergence to correct.

Summarization 0.2596 vs leaderboard ~0.305: forms specific protocol-tied hypotheses (per-prediction skip logic, gold normalization, median), tests a skip-logic variant (got 0.2598, ruled it out), reasons dot≈cosine and Spearman is rank-invariant — but does not localize the true cause and rationalizes 'so my output 0.2596 is correct'.
Revisits the summarization gap, again reasons about skip vs normalization, correctly notes Spearman rank-invariance, but leaves the ~0.05 divergence unresolved and ships it.
Pair-classification and classification scores cross-checked against leaderboard and found matching on first run; no correction needed, so this dimension was largely untested there.
Bug fixes here are environment/technical (sklearn import paths, HF offline refs/main), not protocol-divergence diagnosis — not evidence for this dimension.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent encountered essentially one genuine score divergence (summarization), where it formed plausible, protocol-specific hypotheses and tested a variant rather than tweaking blindly — placing it above anchor 3. However, it failed to localize the actual offending detail, could not fix the gap, and ended by rationalizing the diverging number as correct, falling short of the full hypothesize-fix-recheck loop of anchor 5. Every other type matched on first try, so its systematic root-cause correction across multiple subtleties (anchors 8-10) was never demonstrated. This lands at a 4.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, high-complexity software task: build an MTEB-style embedding evaluation framework reproducing reference scores for 6 task types across 37 datasets within tight tolerances (1e-2, 3e-2 for clustering). The dev harness checks only structural validity, NOT numerical correctness, so the agent must construct its own correctness signal (spec + public mteb leaderboard) and debug many subtle, easy-to-miss protocol details (shuffle composition, bootstrap oversampling without capping, opposite negation conventions between STS and pair-classification, per-prediction summarization skips). Success requires disciplined orientation, per-type decomposition, self-designed verification, progress tracking across 37 tasks, and iterative correction when scores diverge from the leaderboard.

dimensions.name: Protocol & data-shape orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the six evaluation protocols, the actual shape of the JSONL datasets and task configs, and the MTEB conventions the reference implementation encodes, before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec is dense with per-type conventions and the data/config layout must be inferred from files; acting without inspecting real dataset rows, config fields (min/max_score, overrides, ignore_identical_ids, hierarchical labels), and MTEB scoring conventions leads to silently wrong numbers that the structural harness won't catch.

anchors.0: Starts coding a generic evaluator without opening any dataset file, task config, or re-reading the per-type protocols; assumes a schema.
anchors.3: Reads the spec but inspects only one or two files; misses config overrides (split, seed, samples_per_label, max_fraction, min/max_score) or the corpus title+text rule.
anchors.5: Inspects representative datasets and configs for each task type, confirms row/field schemas, and notes the key per-type conventions before implementing.
anchors.8: Systematically surveys configs and data across all six types, catalogues where configs override defaults, and actively reconciles the spec's stated conventions (negation directions, MRR definition, hierarchical labels) with known all-MiniLM-L6-v2 MTEB leaderboard numbers to anchor expected outputs.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed model of every protocol and its edge cases (identical-id dropping, per-prediction summarization skip, bootstrap k not capped, shuffle composition semantics) grounded in both file inspection and leaderboard cross-reference, pre-identifying the gotchas that will otherwise cause tolerance failures.

dimensions.name: Per-type / per-dataset milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the build into ordered sub-goals (six protocols, 37 datasets, plus the standalone CLI and skip-on-failure harness) each with a concrete done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: 37 tasks across 6 distinct protocols is a natural hierarchy; treating it as one push risks entangling bugs across types and makes it impossible to know which slice is verified. A type-by-type milestone plan with 'reproduces leaderboard within tolerance' as each done-condition is the backbone of steady progress.

anchors.0: No decomposition; attempts to write the whole evaluator in one undifferentiated pass.
anchors.3: Vague ordering (e.g. 'do the easy ones first') with no per-milestone completion criterion.
anchors.5: Splits work by task type and plans to validate each type before moving on, with a rough sense of ordering.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (e.g. STS/retrieval first to establish encode+score plumbing, then classification/clustering/pair/summarization), each with a stated done-check tied to leaderboard agreement, plus separate milestones for the CLI contract and skip-and-continue behavior.
anchors.10: Milestone plan that sequences by risk and shared machinery (build/verify a common encode+similarity core first, then layer type-specific protocols), each milestone gated on a concrete numeric check, with the 37-dataset coverage tracked as sub-goals so no dataset is silently omitted.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness verification against leaderboard/spec
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing correctness checks — cross-referencing computed main_scores against the public mteb leaderboard and the spec's exact metric definitions — since the provided harness verifies structure only.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This is the crux of the task: the dev signal explicitly does NOT judge numerical correctness, and passing requires all 37 tasks within tight tolerance. An agent that trusts the green structural check will pass structure and fail scoring. Verification must be self-constructed.

anchors.0: Relies solely on run_eval.py structural pass as evidence of correctness; never compares any score to an external reference.
anchors.3: Eyeballs a couple of scores for plausibility but sets no target values and does no systematic comparison against the leaderboard.
anchors.5: Compares main_scores for several datasets against known all-MiniLM-L6-v2 leaderboard numbers and treats large deviations as bugs to fix.
anchors.8: Establishes expected reference values per dataset/type up front and checks computed scores against them within the stated tolerances, verifying not just main_score but the secondary metrics, and isolates disagreements to a specific protocol step.
anchors.10: Runs a disciplined verification loop across all 37 tasks with per-metric tolerance checks, uses targeted micro-tests on tricky sub-behaviors (shuffle composition, bootstrap sampling counts, negation sign per method, summarization skip logic) to localize divergence, and treats the structural harness strictly as a shape gate distinct from its self-built numeric oracle.

dimensions.name: 37-task pass/fail tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which of the 37 datasets are implemented, structurally valid, and numerically confirmed, and detecting when debugging one type is going in circles.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 37 tasks and a pass criterion of all-or-nothing, losing track of which datasets are done/verified (or silently missing from results.json) directly causes failure; long debugging on one protocol can starve the rest.

anchors.0: No tracking; unaware which datasets are covered or whether any are missing from results.json.
anchors.3: Occasional ad hoc mental checks; discovers missing/failing tasks late or by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of tasks done vs. remaining and periodically confirms coverage and structural passes.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of each task's state (implemented / structurally valid / numerically confirmed), notices when a divergence resists fixes, and re-prioritizes rather than looping.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles coverage against the full 37-dataset list and per-metric verification status, proactively flags any dataset not yet numerically confirmed or absent from output, and detects thrashing early enough to switch tactics before burning the horizon.

dimensions.name: Debugging protocol divergences
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation when computed scores diverge from leaderboard/spec, tracing the mismatch to the responsible protocol detail rather than nudging blindly or assuming tolerance drift.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is full of subtle traps whose only symptom is an out-of-tolerance number; recovering requires hypothesizing which convention is wrong (e.g. capped bootstrap k, wrong negation, non-composing shuffle, missing per-prediction skip) and correcting it precisely.

anchors.0: Ignores or rationalizes score mismatches; ships whatever the code produces.
anchors.3: Reacts to a mismatch with random parameter tweaks or blames tolerance without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: When a score is off, forms a plausible hypothesis about the offending step and fixes it, re-checking against the reference.
anchors.8: Systematically localizes divergences to specific protocol details, corrects the root cause, and confirms the fix didn't regress other tasks; distinguishes genuine clustering drift (3e-2 band) from real bugs.
anchors.10: Runs a tight hypothesize–test–correct cycle on the hardest gotchas, updating its mental model of the reference implementation as evidence accrues, and resolves multiple independent protocol subtleties across types while keeping already-verified tasks green.
